newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dollar/mark clings to support below 1.50.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dollar/mark clings to support below 1.50.

text.p: The dollar failed to hold above 1.50 marks for a second straight session, which likely portends continued near-term losses, despite a stubborn support near 1.4960, technical analysts said on Thursday.
Backup support rests at 1.4920 marks and last week's low at 1.4885, rates which may shortly appear on trading screens, chartists said.
"Dollar/mark looks very weak. We've had a lot of activity in the mark crosses that might be contributing to dollar/mark weakness," said Ben Morden, technical analyst at IDEA Inc.
Dollar/mark may have to wait for dollar/Swiss to slump before it can move lower, chartists said. A slow, but steady rally in mark/Swiss should keep pressure on the greenback.
"Dollar/mark has been leading. New lows on dollar/Swiss would be confirmation, but we haven't gotten it yet," said Morden.
Against the yen, the dollar remains mired in a narrow range, capped by mark/yen's failure to extend a sharp Monday rally past resistance near 74.75, technicians said.
Mark/yen support sits at 73.95 and dollar/yen should sit comfortably for now between 110.80 and 111.80, chartists said.
Sterling remains the forex market darling, blasting past 2.53 marks and $1.69 during intraday trading Thursday.
Chartists said sterling is in a "frictionless" rally, with the latest theoretical resistance points approaching at $1.6930 and 2.5430 marks, a six-year moving average.
"People keep trying to find levels to sell into it, but you have to stay with this thing until it tells you it's time to get out," Solin said. "It's suicide trying to call a top in sterling/mark."
The other major move occurred down under, where the Aussie dollar eclipsed 81 U.S. cents for the first time in six years.
The Aussie has enjoyed solid capital flows as yield-hungry investors leery of the swings in Europe over proposed Economic and Monetary Union have flocked to rich Aussie bond returns.
But the current Aussie uptrend could fall prey to a rising wedge formation, which appears to point at resistance at $0.8170/80, Solin said.
"The ascent of the highs has been slower than the ascent of the lows, which is a termination pattern," Solin said. "Invariably, these break down sharply."
